prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Alder Creek Electrical Distribution Substation supplies distribution circuits via transformer and feeder bays. Automation boundary: bay monitoring/control, station coordination, external interfaces. Primary equipment, protection and field wiring stay under approved designs and operating limits. Elements: Bay Automation Controller (Juniper) does bay sequencing, status evaluation and permissive checks, produces Bay Status Digest, and requests breaker operations from Breaker Control Unit only when mode/permissives allow. North Bay Controller and South Bay Controller automate their station portions. Feeder Protection Relay (Tandem) detects feeder faults, initiates protection in its zone, and produces Relay Diagnostic Note on self-monitoring conditions. Breaker Control Unit executes authorized breaker operations and enforces local interlocks. Station Supervisory Control System (Glasswing) provides the consolidated operator interface (station/bay indications, communication quality; does not replace local indications), supervisory coordination, and produces Alarm Acknowledgement Slip; it performs no protective functions. Station Gateway carries supervisory communications between station-level functions and remote operations interfaces, as the boundary for authorized external connections. Satellite Time Receiver (Bluefin) acquires satellite timing reference, distributes time over the time-distribution network for consistent event timestamps, and produces Clock Drift Snapshot when offset meets reporting condition; provides time-quality indications. Sequence Event Archive retains events. Engineering Workstation: controlled configuration/maintenance. Maintenance Remote Terminal: approved maintenance access only, not local authority. Station DC System supplies control/operating power within design capacity; power loss can interrupt supervisory visibility and time distribution. Actors: Control Room Operator uses supervisory displays, directs operation, and verifies states; Protection Relay Engineer (Larkspur) maintains settings via change process; Substation Field Crew does field work under clearances; Substation Supervisor oversees supervisory system use and escalates availability concerns. Requirements: protection trips independent of bay control; local control takes precedence; remote/supervisory commands subject to permissions, procedures, interlocks and availability; local interlocks are authoritative. Comms loss may make data stale; operators confirm indications are current after recovery. Timestamps aid correlation but do not validate measurements. Loss of timing reference means device holdover, which degrades over time.

New part:
S052: The Feeder Protection Relay provides local protection for its assigned feeder and operates independently of supervisory control availability.
S053: Its approved setting group defines the pickup levels, time delays, and logic required for the feeder protection scheme.
S054: The Protection Relay Engineer develops setting changes against the approved protection study and the current equipment data.
S055: The Protection Relay Engineer documents the engineering basis and expected operational effect for each proposed change.
S056: Engineering Workstation maintains the working configuration under revision control.
S057: Engineering Workstation produces the Settings Review Receipt after a settings review is completed.
S058: Each proposed change receives a unique revision identifier before review begins.
S059: The Protection Relay Engineer verifies that proposed values agree with the approved coordination objectives.
S060: A second qualified reviewer independently checks calculations, logic changes, and device applicability.
S061: The review confirms that the proposed configuration is complete, internally consistent, and suitable for the intended feeder.
S062: Coordination checks consider upstream and downstream protection behavior across the expected operating range.
S063: Protection settings are not approved solely on the basis of copied values from another installation.
S064: Engineering Workstation retains the approved configuration and its revision history for controlled access.
S065: Configuration access is limited to personnel with assigned engineering responsibilities.
S066: The Protection Relay Engineer records the approval status before any setting change is released for implementation.
S067: Before deployment, the approved configuration is checked against the intended device model and firmware version.
S068: A controlled outage or other approved work window is required when implementation could affect feeder protection.
S069: The Substation Field Crew follows the authorized work instructions during device access and setting transfer.
S070: After installation, the implemented values are compared with the approved configuration.
S071: The Feeder Protection Relay is functionally checked to confirm the intended protection behavior after a change.
S072: Any discrepancy stops release of the configuration until its cause is resolved and reviewed.
S073: The Substation Supervisor ensures that engineering changes follow the established authorization and operational control process.
S074: The Substation Field Crew is known operationally as Cinder during field activities.
S075: Cinder performs inspections, maintenance, and switching support within the boundaries of approved work.
S076: Field access begins only after the required work authorization and site entry controls are confirmed.
S077: The Control Room Operator coordinates operational access with the Switching Desk Coordinator before work that could affect energized equipment.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
